[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Maya, I'm the AE on this account, and with me are Diego and Lin from our SE team.
[00:08] Jordan (VP Eng): Hey — Jordan here, thanks. Quick time check, we got about 50 minutes right?
[00:12] Maya (AE): Yep about 50. We'll run through security gating questions, then handoff to Diego for the technical pieces.
[00:18] Priya (Head of Security): Great. Our primary ask up front — are you SOC2 Type II and do you have ISO27001? We need the certs and also details on audit log retention.
[00:26] Diego (SE): Absolutely, we are SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 certified — I'll share the attestations. For audit logs we have per-tenant logging in Dedicated and Private with configurable retention; Hosted has a standard 90-day retention unless you opt-in for longer retention add-on.
[00:40] Sasha (Compliance): Is there a way to export your audit logs to our SIEM — like Splunk or Sumo?
[00:44] Lin (SE): Yes, we support push delivery to SIEMs via secure syslog or our Kafka export. There's also S3 bucket delivery with KMS encryption. Small note: Hosted push delivery requires enterprise add-on — Dedicated/Private can be integrated into your VPC directly.
[01:00] Ethan (Infra Lead): For KMS — our security policy requires customer-managed keys (CMK) and HSM-backed keys for production PII. Can Redwood support BYOK and HSM KMS?
[01:10] Diego (SE): We support customer-managed keys in Dedicated and Private via KMS integrations — in cloud-hosted Dedicated you can configure an AWS KMS CMK or GCP CMEK; for Private/on-prem we can integrate with HSMs through your KMS appliance. Hosted (shared) currently offers server-side encryption with Redwood-managed keys; customer-managed keys aren't supported on the shared multi-tenant Hosted plan for now.
[01:30] Priya: That's a sticking point — our regulators demand CMKs for models that touch PII. If BYOK isn't available on Hosted, that pushes us to Dedicated or Private. What's the timeline to enable CMK for Hosted?
[01:42] Maya: Short answer — Hosted CMK for multi-tenant customers is on the roadmap but not GA. We can detail the product plan, but if CMK is a hard requirement for go-live, Dedicated or Private are the recommended paths.
[01:52] Jordan: Ok. On the RBAC side, we need fine-grained roles mapped to our internal groups — devs, infra, auditors, support. Can we sync SAML groups to Redwood roles and have scoped API keys per role?
[02:04] Lin: Yes, we support SSO with SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning for groups. You can map SAML assertions to Redwood RBAC roles, and you can issue scoped API keys with limited permissions. We also expose token-level scopes in the Console. Small glitch: group rename or SCIM sync delays are possible — sometimes it takes a minute to sync across replicas during heavy loads.
[02:24] Priya: Do you provide session logging for SSO login events and admin actions? Auditors want an immutable trail.
[02:30] Diego: Audit trail is available — admin actions, role changes, API key issuance are logged. For Dedicated/Private you can set up immutable exports to your retention storage; Hosted retains logs and they're viewable in our Console plus exports for the enterprise retention add-on.
[02:44] Sasha: Immutable — can we get write-once storage or legal-hold?
[02:48] Lin: For Private deployments you can attach WORM-enabled S3 or equivalent; for Hosted we offer export to WORM enabled buckets on request as part of a compliance package. We'll need to coordinate legal hold policies together.
[03:00] Jordan: About data residency — we run in EU and US regions; our regs say EU customer data must stay in EU. How does Redwood guarantee residency for inference data?
[03:10] Diego: We can pin requests to a region via routing policy. Dedicated and Private let you specify region and physical VPC placement. Hosted offers region controls but there are caveats with model fallbacks that might route to a replica — we document which models are available in which zones. For strict residency requirements, Private or Dedicated in your EU region is the safe choice.
[03:30] Ethan: Latency tradeoffs — we have latency SLOs for customer-facing flows. How much overhead does RBAC and encryption add?
[03:38] Lin: Encryption is handled at rest and in transit; per-request encryption/decryption for CMK may add negligible latency (single-digit ms) unless you route to HSM for every token key exchange — in that case there can be spikes. For consistent low-latency, we recommend using envelope encryption with local cache of data keys—Redwood's Dedicated runtime handles KV cache to minimize HSM round-trips.
[04:00] Priya: Can you describe the key rotation and access controls for keys? We need proof of separation of duties and key rotation logs.
[04:08] Diego: Keys managed by your KMS follow your policy — rotation is handled at KMS level; Redwood logs key usage and rotation events in audit logs. For Private, your security team can control rotation schedules and we provide a key-usage ledger export for internal audits.
[04:22] Jordan: About model artifacts and training data — we won't let model fine-tuning include customer PII. Will Redwood persist prompt data or model checkpoints?
[04:31] Maya: By default we don't retain prompts beyond short-term caches used for inference; we have explicit data retention settings. For Hosted, there's a default ephemeral cache but customers can opt into retention for evals. For Dedicated/Private, you control persistence. We'll send the data retention whitepaper.
[04:46] Sasha: What about controlled access to logs for auditors? Do you support time-limited auditor roles or auditor API keys?
[04:52] Lin: Yes — you can create time-limited roles and scoped auditor API keys. We recommend short-lived credentials via our SAML/SCIM integration and centralized session logs for traceability.
[05:04] Priya: On SAML — do you support multiple IdPs per customer? We have federated domains.
[05:10] Diego: Multiple IdP support is available in Dedicated/Private. Hosted supports a single primary IdP with a fallback; multi-IdP is part of enterprise configuration.
[05:20] Jordan: For the proposed POC — we'd like to run smoke traffic with synthetic PII to verify end-to-end encryption, KMS integration, and audit exports. Can Redwood provide a staging org?
[05:28] Maya: Yes, we can spin up a hosted staging org or a short-term Dedicated sandbox for the POC. For KMS integration testing we typically recommend Dedicated sandbox so you can validate CMK behavior.
[05:38] Ethan: How much coordination is needed from our infra for Dedicated sandbox? VPC peering, IAM role setup?
[05:44] Lin: We'll need IAM role for the KMS access, VPC peering setup for network isolation, and a small firewall rule set. Diego will put together a checklist.
[05:52] Diego: I'll share a step-by-step for Dedicated sandbox including sample terraform snippets for VPC, IAM, and KMS policy.
[06:00] Priya: One more — vulnerability scanning and pentest cadence?
[06:04] Maya: We run quarterly vulnerability scans and annual third-party pentests; reports are available under NDA. We'll share the summary and a process for on-demand pentest coordination.
[06:15] Sasha: Great. Are you able to provide indemnity and data breach SLA language? Our legal team will need to review.
[06:21] Maya: Yes — for enterprise contracts we have standard breach clauses and incident response SLAs. I'll loop in our legal after this call.
[06:30] Jordan: On pricing — Dedicated committed capacity vs Private one-time license + support — can you give ballpark? We just want rough order before finance deep-dive.
[06:38] Maya: High level: Dedicated is usage + reservation model — predictable monthly for reserved GPU pools; Private has larger upfront platform fee plus ongoing support. Diego will provide a tailored estimate based on your throughput numbers.
[06:50] Ethan: Our throughput: expected 30 requests/s at p95 latency under 600ms for typical 512 token prompts. Will Redwood Dedicated hit that?
[06:58] Diego: Yes, with proper autoscaling and batch sizing Dedicated can meet that — we'll run a capacity estimate based on request size/seq len distribution. If you want, we can include target batch sizes and kernel optimizations in the technical proposal.
[07:12] Priya: On data deletion — if we terminate, how fast do you purge data and can we get a certificate of deletion?
[07:18] Lin: We have deletion workflows — standard deletion within 30 days, expedited deletion with certificate as part of enterprise agreement. For Private, you can control immediate wipe.
[07:30] Jordan: Any known limitations with HIPAA or healthcare workloads?
[07:34] Maya: Redwood can support HIPAA workloads on Dedicated/Private with BAAs; Hosted has constraints. We'll share the HIPAA readiness doc.
[07:44] Priya: Can we get a brief on how rollback/fallback works in cross-region outages? Auditors ask about graceful degradation.
[07:52] Diego: We have smart routing — fallbacks can route to a compatible model variant in another region, but that may affect residency. For strict residency you can opt out of cross-region fallbacks and accept degraded availability instead. We can show policy configs.
[08:08] Jordan: Good to know. For the POC let's aim for Dedicated sandbox in EU, CMK integration, and audit exports to our S3 WORM bucket.
[08:16] Maya: Noted. I'll capture that as the primary POC scope.
[08:20] Sasha: Anything else from Redwood?
[08:22] Diego: I'll highlight potential performance caveats with HSM-backed key operations and propose envelope key caching to minimize latency.
[08:30] Priya: We'll send over our retention matrix and list of auditors.
[08:34] Maya: Perfect. We'll follow up with the attestation docs and a tailor-made proposal.
[08:40] Jordan: Thanks everyone. Back channels if needed.
[08:44] Maya: Thanks all — we'll send docs today and propose times for the finance deep-dive next week.
